title: Hemispheric failover orchestrator with stream stitching and SLO-aware shedding
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Design and implement an active-active hemispheric failover orchestrator for Redwood's hosted API edge layer that preserves streaming session continuity. The feature will provide automated traffic shifting between region clusters (e.g., us-east / eu-west hemispheres), SLO-aware circuit breakers, and a lightweight stream-stitching protocol to allow clients to reattach or gracefully continue long-lived streams after an inter-region handoff. The goal is to maintain p99/p95 latency and availability SLOs during partial-region degradations while limiting cost and KV-sync overhead. This ticket covers design, prototype, e2e tests, and canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Documentation: design doc and runbook published to Confluence (confluence.redwood.com/display/RN/Hemispheric+Failover)
Successful simulated regional outage (chaos test) without >1% increase in failed stream reconnects after implementing stitch protocol
SLO compliance: p95 end-user latency degradation < 25% and availability >= 99.9% during single-region degraded mode under baseline load
Circuit breaker triggers and automated traffic redistribution validated in staging with synthetic traffic spike
Canary rollout steps produce no alerts at 10% / 50% / 100% phases and perf dashboards show expected KV-sync overhead < 3% tail latency impact
End-to-end integration tests for stitch tokens, resume_nonce and KV snapshot restore pass in CI (integration-hemispheric-suite)
implementation_notes: Orchestrator service: new lightweight controller (hemispheric-orch) that subscribes to region health, SLO telemetry, and capacity hints
Traffic policy: define weighted hemispheric routing policy with drain windows and exponential backoff for live streams

Stream stitching protocol: generate 'stitch_token' + resume_nonce on initial connection; client SDKs supplied with reattach API that uses stitch_token to negotiate resumption; server must validate token and reconcile KV snapshot sequence_number
KV sync: implement delta-based heartbeat snapshots (heartbeat-snapshots) to reduce cross-region bandwidth; use sequence_number checkpoints rather than full model KV copies
Circuit breaker rules: error_rate > 3% OR p95 latency > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive 1-min buckets triggers region soft-isolation; hard-isolation if >5% errors for 5 min
Load shedding: SLO-first policy — shed non-critical/low-tier requests first (client-tier header), prefer graceful tail drop with early finish, and send explicit 429+Retry-After with reason codes

Proxy handshake: ephemeral session proxies will accept client stream and forward to primary region while capturing KV checkpoints; on failover, new region reads last checkpoint and applies missing deltas before issuing resume instruction
Telemetry: add per-stitch metrics (stitch_success, stitch_latency, stitch_reconnects) and annotate traces with stitch_token for debugging
Backwards compatibility: fall back to full reconnect if client does not support stitch_token; orchestrator must detect and handle both flows
Security: stitch_token short TTL (60s) and bound to client certificate or API key to prevent replay; include audit log event for each stitch

risk: Complexity of KV delta reconciliation introduces tail latency risk; stitch_token security must be airtight to avoid session hijack. Operational risk: debugging cross-region reattachments requires richer traces and tooling. We mitigate with short TTLs, HMAC verification, and initial conservative canary windows.
